summary: Review round 2's finding is fixed: the stalled rebuild's 200 degraded was decided before the durable consumer's checks, so a durable that was gone or unbound answered 200 and named the wrong fault. The stall branch is now the last decision, below every 503 check, with a test that holds a stall past the grace plus a recreated durable at 503; the five comment corrections, the changelog fragment's log lines and the four missing census rows go with it, and main is merged forward once more so this head's CI carries #2516's envoy-go-race-docs job.

proof.criterion: Review round 2's finding: while a stall is past bus.RepairGrace, a durable consumer that is gone, unbound or silent must still answer 503, and 200 degraded must be the answer only when nothing worse holds.
proof.surface: The in-process cmd/listener test over a real embedded NATS, a real durable and the real interest and session caches, driving healthzHandler through httptest - the rig the rest of the file uses, with recreateListenerDurable from durable_unbound_test.go producing the unbound durable.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go test ./cmd/listener/ -run 'HookStall' -count=1 -timeout 10m, first with the stall branch in its old place above the durable checks, then with it below them.
proof.observed: Old place: FAIL TestHealthzReportsARecreatedDurableThroughAHookStall, '/healthz with the durable recreated a whole bus.RepairGrace into the stall = 200 map[error:KV watch rebuild unavailable: ... status:degraded], want 503 unhealthy with error "durable consumer unavailable: not bound to this listener's subscription"'. Below them: ok, and the test logs the 503 it wanted. The degraded-only case still answers 200 degraded, and the zero-stall lock still holds.
proof.negativeControl: The branch in its old place is the control, and it is exactly the code the reviewer read at 806dbdaf: the new test fails there and passes only with the branch moved.

proof.criterion: The behaviour the issue is about is unchanged by the move: a stalled rebuild with everything else healthy is still 200 degraded naming the KV watch rebuild, under the grace the answer is unchanged, and the caches follow their buckets again when the fault lifts.
proof.surface: The built envoy-listener binary against a real nats-server v2.10.29 with JetStream, restarted under a configuration denying only $JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.KV_envoy_{interests,roles,sessions}.>; /healthz and GET /v1/interests/ over HTTP.
proof.observed: 200 healthy at start and after a plain NATS restart with the interest written then served and 0 ERROR lines; with the deny in place 200 healthy inside the grace, then 200 {"error":"KV watch rebuild unavailable: rewatch interest cache: watch interest registry KV bucket: context deadline exceeded\nrewatch session cache: watch session registry KV bucket: context deadline exceeded (no rebuild has succeeded for 1m0s)","status":"degraded"}; 200 healthy again once the deny was lifted, with a new interest served.
proof.negativeControl: At this branch's base 88840d35, as Go probes in a throwaway copy of the tree: TestBaseHealthzAnswersAHookStallPastAMinute fails ('/healthz 75 s into a rebuild that never succeeded = 200 map[... status:healthy]') and TestBaseRewatchRetryAfterAReconnectLogsNoError fails on the ERROR the base logs for a rewatch the retry repairs.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 3 and 4a at the head that merges: 200 of 200 isolated runs of TestListenerFollowsTheInterestRegistryAcrossNATSRestarts, and the suites green.
proof.surface: The listener's own harness against a real NATS, and the repository's Go test harness for the packages this round touches.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/cmd/listener && go test -c -o "$TMPDIR/listener-r5b.test" . && 200 serial runs of "$TMPDIR/listener-r5b.test" -test.run '^TestListenerFollowsTheInterestRegistryAcrossNATSRestarts$' -test.count=1; and cd packages/envoy && go build ./... && go vet ./internal/bus/ ./internal/kvwatch/ ./cmd/listener/ && go test -p 2 -parallel 4 ./cmd/listener/ -count=1 -skip '<the four Docker-only TestDispatch tests>' && go test -p 2 -parallel 4 ./internal/bus/ ./internal/kvwatch/ -count=1
proof.observed: 200 PASS, 0 FAIL at 0ae1b454, and the same at a7e0ec2a before the merge. build and vet exit 0; ok cmd/listener 466.318s, ok internal/bus 301.240s, ok internal/kvwatch 63.171s. Test runs are bounded as the architect asked after tonight's OOM kills (-p 2 -parallel 4, one suite group at a time, no parallel subagents running suites); the pod's memory.usage_in_bytes read 2.84 GiB before the listener suite.
proof.negativeControl: The same loop with 49 runs at the base 88840d35: 48 PASS, 1 FAIL, the failure being this issue's symptom (ERROR envoy nats reconnect hook failed ... rewatch session cache: open session registry KV bucket: context deadline exceeded).

proof.criterion: The forward merge for #2516's new CI job changes none of this branch's lines, so it is a confirmation rather than a new round of change.
proof.surface: The branch's own diff against its base, by the unchanged-diff fingerprint every role compares.
proof.command: jj diff --from "fork_point(main@origin | <head>)" --to <head> --git --context 0 '~(.legion | docs/solutions)' | sed -e '/^@@/d' -e '/^index /d' | sha256sum, at a7e0ec2a and again at 0ae1b454
proof.observed: 47ab5624dc663451d608e524740406494f5395764431108c7035e1ee10d4b818 on both sides; the merge conflicted with nothing. The suites and the smoke above were re-run at the merge head all the same.
proof.negativeControl: The two earlier forward merges are the contrast: each moved the fingerprint (7bf2162e to 40e2f17a, and b2166d30 to 2538a250), and each was treated as a full round by the tester.

filesChanged: packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go: the HookStall branch moved below every 503 check, so it is the last decision before the 200 healthy answer; its inline comment is one line, and the handler's doc comment states the order and why.

packages/envoy/cmd/listener/healthz_hook_stall_test.go: the rig is a fixture both tests share, and TestHealthzReportsARecreatedDurableThroughAHookStall holds a stall past the grace with a recreated durable at 503.

packages/envoy/internal/bus/hook_stall_test.go, internal/bus/nats.go, internal/bus/recovery.go, internal/kvwatch/kvwatch.go, packages/envoy/AGENTS.md: the five comment corrections the review asked for (the 503 wording in the test comments, HookStall's doc for a run an event overtook, what the AWS filter actually matches, and the stale main.go line citations replaced by rewatchListenerKVWatchers called from rebuildListenerDependencies).
packages/envoy/.changes/unreleased/INFRA-743-rewatch-retry-report.yaml: the two log lines an operator's filter reads, the new stall_ms attribute, and the removal of the reason 'repair failed'.
No file changed in the merge 0ae1b454; it conflicted with nothing.
trickyParts: The order of /healthz's branches is the contract now: every 503 check runs before the stall, and the stall is the last decision before the healthy answer. The new test is what pins it, and INFRA-594's implementer has the full order in writing, since #2446 edits the same handler.
discoveredComplexity: The Envoy hub was recreated twice tonight, so three publishes of the /healthz ordering to INFRA-594 were refused ('nats: outbound buffer limit exceeded'); it went on Dispatch as comment 60515838 and was re-sent when the bus answered. INFRA-594's implementer has confirmed it.
#2446 is still open and edits this handler; its own 503 'role lane subscription inactive' branch belongs with the other 503 checks, above the stall.
